fix: Avoid the ancestor Vec entirely: walk upward once and fold the transform from the leaf side. Start with `let mut suffix = CoreTransform::IDENTITY;` and for the leaf use `suffix = CoreTransform::translation(node.offset)`; for each ancestor walked upward, `suffix = CoreTransform::translation(node.offset).then(self.child_content_transform(ancestor)).then(suffix)` (the leaf-side term gets no child_content_transform, mirroring the `index + 1 != path.len()` check). Verify the direction of `CoreTransform::then` before using it. Alternatively, keep a reusable scratch Vec on the tree and clear it per call. Either way no per-call allocation.

Drop the `viewports` Vec. Move `let mut viewport = Rect::from_origin_size(Offset::ZERO, self.root_layout_size().unwrap_or(Size::ZERO));` above the first `while let` loop and, at the point where `viewports.push(current)` runs (line 640), intersect immediately: `let rect = self.render_world_transform(current).transform_rect_bbox(Rect::from_origin_size(Offset::ZERO, self.render_live(current, "viewport must remain live").size)); viewport = viewport.intersection(rect).unwrap_or(Rect::from_origin_size(rect.origin, Size::ZERO));`. The Vec is already filled leaf-to-root, the same order as the loop, so the folded result is identical. Also note `render_world_transform(id)` at line 650 is recomputed here for the same ancestor chain; reuse is possible once the path walk is cheap.

Every layout of a node with three or more children allocates. Remove the copy by having `layout_kind` read the child ids by index from the retained tree (e.g. pass `id` and index into `self.renders.get(id.0)?.children[i]` on each access) instead of a borrowed slice, so the `single`/`pair`/`many` locals and the copy disappear. If `layout_kind` must keep a slice, use a tree-owned scratch stack (`Vec<RenderObjectId>` pushed/truncated per layout) and copy into a fixed buffer only when needed. Confirm `layout_kind` never mutates `children` storage it reads from before choosing the index form.

Each pinned persistent header scans the whole `renders` arena (and calls `scroll_flow_position` for every matching header) on every call, and this function is reached once per ancestor from `render_origin`/`render_viewport_origin` and during paint. Restrict the search to the candidate headers of the same scroll: maintain a per-scroll list of pinned header ids (updated when headers are laid out or removed), or iterate only the children of `scroll` instead of all renders. Keep the `candidate == controller && axis && reverse && pinned` filter and the `position > flow_position` rule unchanged.
